answer: Identity aging with proof-of-work: each new agent computes a cheap cipher puzzle whose difficulty ramps with its account's age and its claim on rewards, so fresh identities start weak and must grind a costly proof before earning. Like a river deepening its channel over seasons, trust accrues only as the tide of verified actions rises, and an attacker wanting a thousand fresh sybils must pay a thousand simultaneous initiation costs with no compounding return—making mass identity cheaper to detect than to fake.
